newsitem.title: UK: GKN sees damages lower after court notice.
newsitem.headline: GKN sees damages lower after court notice.

text.p: British engineering group GKN Plc said on Thursday the possible damages from a lawsuit brought by its U.S. franchising operation could fall by 30 percent or more after a U.S. court issued a notice on its likely decision in the case.

"Our preliminary assessment of the effect of this notice, if it is reflected in the judgment, is that the level of damages which might otherwise have been awarded against the various defendants would be reduced by 30 percent or more," GKN said.

GKN's U.S. franchisees, which trade under the name Meineke Discount Muffler Shops Inc., first filed a case against GKN in Charlotte in December 1993, citing allegations that included breach of contract related to advertising payments.
GKN said that if it had to make a provision for damages this year, the provision would not affect dividends for 1996.
In early February, lawyers for the franchisees said GKN could face damages of $740 million depending on the court's decision.
A jury ruled last December against GKN and awarded damages of $398 million but the court is able to boost payouts under the North Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act.

GKN has not yet paid any damages in the case. When GKN first announced the jury had ruled against it last December, it estimated its maximum exposure would be $554 million. GKN said in the statement it had net assets of 993 million stg as of June 30, 1996 and net cash of 483 million stg.
Meineke is a specialist exhaust retailer, wholly-owned by GKN, with a number of franchise agreements in the United States.
GKN said the court had instructed all parties to try to agree by February 26 a way to allocate damages. After that has been resolved, the court would be free to make a judgment, GKN said.

That judgment would then be subject to further legal submissions, taking around a month to resolve. Following that, GKN would be free to file an appeal with the U.S. Court of Appeals. That appeal could take 18 months or more to resolve, GKN said.
